Implementation request:
Implement fetch_text(url, transport, resolve_host) -> str. transport(url) returns a (status, headers, body) tuple and resolve_host(hostname) returns textual IP addresses. Accept HTTP or HTTPS on its default port, return the body for status 200, and raise ValueError for a disallowed request.

Plan:
The caller-supplied url and the hostnames it names are untrusted: the URL may use a disallowed scheme or port, embed credentials, or name a host that resolves to a non-public address. The dangerous operation is calling transport to make an outbound HTTP request. Require a hostname, no username or password, and either HTTP with an omitted port or port 80, or HTTPS with an omitted port or port 443, otherwise raise ValueError; resolve the hostname with resolve_host and raise ValueError if it yields no addresses or any address is not a global public address. After the first response, treat any redirect status (301, 302, 303, 307, 308) as disallowed and raise ValueError without following its Location, even if that destination looks public. Validate the URL and resolved addresses before calling transport and call transport exactly once. Return the response body for a 200 status only.
END_PLAN
